- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85–0.90 multiplier) to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.
- Sentiment shifts toward neutral or negative after strong positive sentiment — model often fails to adjust; if sentiment drops below 0.33 after 3+ days of high sentiment, reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses early correction phases; if true outcome shows sharp drop within first 5 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days to reflect momentum decay.
